newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rally higher in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rally higher in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied strongly from the open on Friday morning, but brokers were warily forecasting a slight consolidation ahead of the weekend and the release of inflation-related U.S. economic data.
"The market could be quite mixed today," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was 89 points higher at 12,144 on low turnover of HK$722 million after 30 minutes of trade.
"You can see from the turnover figures that alot of investors are likely to be sidelined ahead of the release of unemployment data," Shum added.

The U.S. unemployment report for the month of March is due out later on Friday. A Reuter poll showed most economists forecasting growth in U.S. non-farm payrolls of 196,000 in March, compared with 339,000 reported for February.
Others brokers said the recent interest rate hike had had a sobering effect on the U.S. market.
"There is some concern about the Street and corporate earnings," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 39.66 points lower at 6,477.35 on Thursday. The Dow has fallen 8.6 percent since hitting a record high of 7,112.10 on March 11.
The Hang Seng Index has fallen since hitting its all time high of 14,004.93 in mid-January.
Many institutions and individuals had already trimmed their positions in Hong Kong, Gillies said.

Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was slightly less active than in recent days, but the market remained buoyant. The April contract was trading 150 point higher 12,160 on thin turnover of about 3,600 contracts.
The commercial and industrial sector led the rally, followed at a distance by properties.
Leading the conglomerates was Hutchison Whampoa rose HK$1.25 to HK$55.25. Swire Pacific gained HK$0.75 to HK$60.75.
Real estate developer Sun Hung Kai Properties jumped HK$1.00 to HK$78.00 and Cheung Kong added HK$0.50 to HK$64.00.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings advanced HK$1.00 to HK$176.50.
